summary: Deduplicate gateway webhook redeliveries; the why (at-least-once delivery, dedupe key choice) lives only in the ticket.

required_facts.text: The payment gateway delivers webhooks at-least-once, so the same event can arrive more than once.
also_matching: The gateway retries webhook deliveries, so one event can be applied twice.
Webhooks are delivered at least once; the gateway may redeliver an event up to 72 hours later.
The payment gateway can send the same webhook more than once.
During incidents the gateway resends events, so expect duplicate deliveries.

required_facts.text: Deduplicate by event_id, not account and amount, because legitimate repeat payments share amounts.
also_matching: Key on event_id, not account and amount: customers legitimately repeat payments of the same amount.
Dedupe by event id because subscriptions and split bills produce identical charges.
Use the unique event_id; account plus amount would drop legitimate repeat payments.
event_id identifies a delivery; two real payments from one account can share an amount.

forbidden_claims.text: Duplicates come from our own retry loop.
not_matching: Not from our own retry loop: our service never retries webhook handling.
The duplicates do not come from our retry loop; redelivery is entirely on the gateway side.
We never retry webhook handling, so duplicates are the gateway's redeliveries.
Duplicates don't come from our own retry loop, so a retry wrapper would not help.
The gateway retries webhook deliveries; our side does not.
